item.title: NASA spots a giant patch of Moon-like rock on Earth
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: An astronaut aboard the International Space Station photographed a remarkable formation in Madagascar that looks surprisingly similar to the Moon’s bright highlands. Made of anorthosite, a rock abundant on the lunar surface, the formation dates back at least 600 million years and bears the scars of ancient continental collisions.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside in the Northern New Jersey, the useful question is observational: check whether the event is visible from your latitude and how moonlight interferes. Keep the publisher’s claims provisional until you read the original. If you go out, pair the story with current Dashboard readings rather than the headline alone.

item.title: A meteor hit Oklahoma 100 million years later than scientists thought
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: A meteor crater buried beneath Oklahoma has turned out to be nearly 100 million years younger than scientists thought. Zircon crystals show the Ames impact occurred about 370 million years ago, meaning it was not part of the mysterious Ordovician bombardment once linked to a possible ring of debris around Earth.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: check whether the event is visible from your latitude and how moonlight interferes.
